\[
I_{\text{out}} = T(I),
\qquad
T(k) = 255 \cdot \frac{1}{N} \sum_{j=0}^{k} h_j
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(h_j\): The number of pixels at level j
- \(N\): The number of pixels
- \(T\): The transfer curve

h_j is the number of pixels at level j and N the number of pixels. T is the cumulative histogram scaled to 0 to 255, the histogram equalization of Gonzalez and Woods. A level shared by many pixels gets a big step up the curve, so crowded ranges spread out. The values stay unrounded until the end. The darkest level that occurs maps to 255 times its share of the pixels, not always to 0. OpenCV's equalizeHist shifts the curve so that it does. Values between two levels take the output interpolated between them.
